passages.text: After some time, David’s son Amnon fell in love with Tamar, the beautiful sister of David’s son Absalom.
passages.sermon:
David had a son named Amnon.
David had another son named Absalom.
Absalom had a sister named Tamar.
Tamar was very beautiful.
After some time, Amnon fell in love with Tamar.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י אַֽחֲרֵי־ כֵ֗ן וּלְאַבְשָׁל֧וֹם בֶּן־ דָּוִ֛ד אָח֥וֹת יָפָ֖ה וּשְׁמָ֣הּ תָּמָ֑ר וַיֶּאֱהָבֶ֖הָ אַמְנ֥וֹן בֶּן־ דָּוִֽד׃

passages.text: Amnon was sick with frustration over his sister Tamar, for she was a virgin, and it seemed implausible for him to do anything to her.
passages.sermon:
Amnon was David’s son.
Tamar was Amnon’s sister.
Tamar was a virgin.
Amnon felt frustrated because of Tamar.
Amnon wanted to do something to Tamar.
Amnon could not find a way to do anything to her.
It seemed impossible to Amnon.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֨צֶר לְאַמְנ֜וֹן לְהִתְחַלּ֗וֹת בַּֽעֲבוּר֙ תָּמָ֣ר אֲחֹת֔וֹ כִּ֥י בְתוּלָ֖ה הִ֑יא וַיִּפָּלֵא֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י אַמְנ֔וֹן לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לָ֖הּ מְאֽוּמָה׃

passages.text: Now Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, the son of David’s brother Shimeah. Jonadab was a very shrewd man, so he asked Amnon, “Why are you, the son of the king, so depressed morning after morning? Won’t you tell me?” Amnon replied, “I am in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.”
passages.sermon:
Amnon was the son of King David.
Amnon had a friend named Jonadab.
Jonadab was the son of Shimeah.
Shimeah was David’s brother.
Jonadab was a very shrewd man.
Jonadab spoke to Amnon.
Jonadab asked, “Why are you, the king’s son, so downcast every morning?”
Jonadab said, “Will you not tell me the reason?”
Amnon answered Jonadab.
Amnon said, “I am in love with Tamar.”
Tamar is the sister of Absalom, my brother.
passages.original: וּלְאַמְנ֣וֹן רֵ֗עַ וּשְׁמוֹ֙ יֽוֹנָדָ֔ב בֶּן־ שִׁמְעָ֖ה אֲחִ֣י דָוִ֑ד וְי֣וֹנָדָ֔ב אִ֥ישׁ חָכָ֖ם מְאֹֽד׃ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ מַדּ֣וּעַ אַ֠תָּה כָּ֣כָה דַּ֤ל בֶּן־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֔קֶר הֲל֖וֹא תַּגִּ֣יד לִ֑י וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אַמְנ֔וֹן אֶת־ תָּמָ֗ר אֲח֛וֹת אַבְשָׁלֹ֥ם אָחִ֖י אֲנִ֥י אֹהֵֽב׃

passages.text: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend you are ill. When your father comes to see you, say to him, ‘Please let my sister Tamar come and give me something to eat. Let her prepare it in my sight so I may watch her and eat it from her hand.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jonadab was Amnon’s friend.
Jonadab was very shrewd.
Jonadab spoke to Amnon.
Jonadab said, “Lie down on your bed.
Pretend you are sick.
Your father will come to see you.
When your father arrives, speak to him.
Say, ‘Please let my sister Tamar come.
Let her give me food to eat.
Let her prepare the food where I can see her.
I want to watch her make it.
I will eat the food from her hand.’”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ יְה֣וֹנָדָ֔ב שְׁכַ֥ב עַל־ מִשְׁכָּבְךָ֖ וְהִתְחָ֑ל וּבָ֧א אָבִ֣יךָ לִרְאוֹתֶ֗ךָ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֡יו תָּ֣בֹא נָא֩ תָמָ֨ר אֲחוֹתִ֜י וְתַבְרֵ֣נִי לֶ֗חֶם וְעָשְׂתָ֤ה לְעֵינַי֙ אֶת־ הַבִּרְיָ֔ה לְמַ֙עַן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶרְאֶ֔ה וְאָכַלְתִּ֖י מִיָּדָֽהּ׃

passages.text: So Amnon lay down and feigned illness. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please let my sister Tamar come and make a couple of cakes in my sight, so that I may eat from her hand.”
passages.sermon:
Amnon was the son of King David.
Amnon lay down on his bed.
Amnon pretended to be sick.
King David came to see Amnon.
Amnon spoke to King David.
Amnon said, “Please let my sister Tamar come.”
Amnon asked Tamar to make two cakes while he watched.
Amnon wanted to eat the cakes from Tamar’s hand.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב אַמְנ֖וֹן וַיִּתְחָ֑ל וַיָּבֹ֨א הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לִרְאֹת֗וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אַמְנ֤וֹן אֶל־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ תָּֽבוֹא־ נָ֞א תָּמָ֣ר אֲחֹתִ֗י וּתְלַבֵּ֤ב לְעֵינַי֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י לְבִב֔וֹת וְאֶבְרֶ֖ה מִיָּדָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Then David sent word to Tamar at the palace: “Please go to the house of Amnon your brother and prepare a meal for him.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king and the father of Tamar and Amnon.
Tamar was David’s daughter.
Amnon was David’s son and Tamar’s brother.
David sent a message to Tamar at the palace.
He told her, “Go to the house of your brother Amnon.”
He told her, “Prepare a meal for him.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח דָּוִ֛ד אֶל־ תָּמָ֖ר הַבַּ֣יְתָה לֵאמֹ֑ר לְכִ֣י נָ֗א בֵּ֚ית אַמְנ֣וֹן אָחִ֔יךְ וַעֲשִׂי־ ל֖וֹ הַבִּרְיָֽה׃

passages.text: So Tamar went to the house of her brother Amnon, who was lying down. She took some dough, kneaded it, made cakes in his sight, and baked them.
passages.sermon:
Tamar was the sister of Amnon.
Amnon was lying down in his house.
Tamar went to Amnon’s house.
Tamar took some dough.
Tamar kneaded the dough.
Tamar made cakes while Amnon watched.
Tamar baked the cakes.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֣לֶךְ תָּמָ֗ר בֵּ֛ית אַמְנ֥וֹן אָחִ֖יהָ וְה֣וּא שֹׁכֵ֑ב וַתִּקַּ֨ח אֶת־ הַבָּצֵ֤ק וַתָּלוֹשׁ וַתְּלַבֵּ֣ב לְעֵינָ֔יו וַתְּבַשֵּׁ֖ל אֶת־ הַלְּבִבֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Then she brought the pan and set it down before him, but he refused to eat. “Send everyone away!” said Amnon. And everyone went out.
passages.sermon:
Tamar was the daughter of King David.
Amnon was Tamar’s brother.
Tamar brought the pan to Amnon.
She set the pan down in front of Amnon.
Amnon refused to eat the food.
Amnon spoke to the people in the room.
Amnon said, “Send everyone away from me.”
All the people left Amnon’s presence.
passages.original: וַתִּקַּ֤ח אֶת־ הַמַּשְׂרֵת֙ וַתִּצֹ֣ק לְפָנָ֔יו וַיְמָאֵ֖ן לֶאֱכ֑וֹל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַמְנ֗וֹן הוֹצִ֤יאוּ כָל־ אִישׁ֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י וַיֵּצְא֥וּ כָל־ אִ֖ישׁ מֵעָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring the food into the bedroom, so that I may eat it from your hand.” Tamar took the cakes she had made and went to her brother Amnon’s bedroom.
passages.sermon:
Amnon was Tamar’s brother.
Amnon spoke to Tamar.
He said, “Bring the food into the bedroom.”
He said, “I want to eat it from your hand.”
Tamar took the cakes she had made.
Tamar went to Amnon’s bedroom.
Tamar brought the cakes to her brother Amnon.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אַמְנ֜וֹן אֶל־ תָּמָ֗ר הָבִ֤יאִי הַבִּרְיָה֙ הַחֶ֔דֶר וְאֶבְרֶ֖ה מִיָּדֵ֑ךְ וַתִּקַּ֣ח תָּמָ֗ר אֶת־ הַלְּבִבוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔תָה וַתָּבֵ֛א לְאַמְנ֥וֹן אָחִ֖יהָ הֶחָֽדְרָה׃

passages.text: And when she had brought them to him to eat, he took hold of her and said, “Come lie with me, my sister!”
passages.sermon:
Tamar was a woman.
Amnon was her brother.
Tamar brought food to Amnon.
She brought the food so he could eat.
Amnon grabbed Tamar.
Amnon said to Tamar, "Come lie with me, my sister."
passages.original: וַתַּגֵּ֥שׁ אֵלָ֖יו לֶֽאֱכֹ֑ל וַיַּֽחֲזֶק־ בָּהּ֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָ֔הּ בּ֛וֹאִי שִׁכְבִ֥י עִמִּ֖י אֲחוֹתִֽי׃

passages.text: “No, my brother!” she cried. “Do not humiliate me, for such a thing should never be done in Israel. Do not do this disgraceful thing!
passages.sermon:
Tamar was a young woman in Israel.
Amnon was her brother.
Amnon wanted to do something wrong to Tamar.
Tamar spoke to Amnon.
She said, “No, my brother!”
She told him, “Do not humiliate me.”
She said, “Such a thing should never be done in Israel.”
She said, “Do not do this disgraceful thing.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ אַל־ אָחִי֙ אַל־ תְּעַנֵּ֔נִי כִּ֛י לֹא־ יֵֽעָשֶׂ֥ה כֵ֖ן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אַֽל־ תַּעֲשֵׂ֖ה אֶת־ הַנְּבָלָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: Where could I ever take my shame? And you would be like one of the fools in Israel! Please speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you.”
passages.sermon:
Tamar was a woman in Israel.  
Amnon was her brother.  
Amnon wanted to do a disgraceful thing to Tamar.  
Tamar spoke to Amnon.  
She said, "Where could I take my shame?"  
She said, "You would become like one of the fools in Israel."  
She said, "Please speak to the king."  
She said, "He will not withhold me from you."
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֗י אָ֤נָה אוֹלִיךְ֙ אֶת־ חֶרְפָּתִ֔י וְאַתָּ֗ה תִּהְיֶ֛ה כְּאַחַ֥ד הַנְּבָלִ֖ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעַתָּה֙ דַּבֶּר־ נָ֣א אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֛י לֹ֥א יִמְנָעֵ֖נִי מִמֶּֽךָּ׃

passages.text: But Amnon refused to listen to her, and being stronger, he violated her and lay with her.
passages.sermon:
Amnon was the son of King David.
Tamar was his sister.
Tamar pleaded with Amnon not to harm her.
Amnon refused to listen to Tamar.
Amnon was stronger than Tamar.
Amnon overpowered Tamar.
Amnon violated Tamar.
Amnon lay with Tamar.
passages.original: וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לִשְׁמֹ֣עַ בְּקוֹלָ֑הּ וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק מִמֶּ֙נָּה֙ וַיְעַנֶּ֔הָ וַיִּשְׁכַּ֖ב אֹתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Then Amnon hated Tamar with such intensity that his hatred was greater than the love he previously had. “Get up!” he said to her. “Be gone!”
passages.sermon:
Amnon was the son of King David.
Tamar was his half-sister.
Amnon hated Tamar.
His hatred was very great.
Amnon’s hatred for Tamar became stronger than the love he once felt for her.
Amnon spoke to Tamar.
He said, “Get up.”
He said, “Go away.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׂנָאֶ֣הָ אַמְנ֗וֹן שִׂנְאָה֙ גְּדוֹלָ֣ה מְאֹ֔ד כִּ֣י גְדוֹלָ֗ה הַשִּׂנְאָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שְׂנֵאָ֔הּ מֵאַהֲבָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲהֵבָ֑הּ וַֽיֹּאמֶר־ לָ֥הּ אַמְנ֖וֹן ק֥וּמִי לֵֽכִי׃

passages.text: “No,” she replied, “sending me away is worse than this great wrong you have already done to me!” But he refused to listen to her.
passages.sermon:
Tamar was the daughter of King David.
Amnon, her half-brother, had just violated her.
Tamar spoke to Amnon.
She said, “Do not send me away.”
She said, “Sending me away is a greater wrong than what you have already done to me.”
Amnon refused to listen to Tamar.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ אַל־ אוֹדֹ֞ת הָרָעָ֤ה הַגְּדוֹלָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את מֵאַחֶ֛רֶת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשִׂ֥יתָ עִמִּ֖י לְשַׁלְּחֵ֑נִי וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לִשְׁמֹ֥עַֽ לָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Instead, he called to his attendant and said, “Throw this woman out and bolt the door behind her!”
passages.sermon:
Amnon was the son of King David.
Amnon had just mistreated his sister Tamar.
Amnon called his attendant.
Amnon gave a command to his attendant.
He said, “Send this woman away from me.”
He said, “Put her outside.”
He said, “Shut the door behind her.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֶֽת־ נַעֲרוֹ֙ מְשָׁ֣רְת֔וֹ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁלְחוּ־ נָ֥א אֶת־ זֹ֛את מֵעָלַ֖י הַח֑וּצָה וּנְעֹ֥ל הַדֶּ֖לֶת אַחֲרֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: So Amnon’s attendant threw her out and bolted the door behind her. Now Tamar was wearing a robe of many colors, because this is what the king’s virgin daughters wore.
passages.sermon:
Tamar was a daughter of King David.
Tamar was a virgin.
Tamar wore a robe of many colors.
The king’s virgin daughters wore robes like this.
Amnon’s attendant took Tamar outside.
The attendant threw Tamar out.
The attendant shut the door behind her.
The attendant locked the door.
passages.original: וְעָלֶ֙יהָ֙ כְּתֹ֣נֶת פַּסִּ֔ים כִּי֩ כֵ֨ן תִּלְבַּ֧שְׁןָ בְנוֹת־ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ הַבְּתוּלֹ֖ת מְעִילִ֑ים וַיֹּצֵ֨א אוֹתָ֤הּ מְשָֽׁרְתוֹ֙ הַח֔וּץ וְנָעַ֥ל הַדֶּ֖לֶת אַחֲרֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: And Tamar put ashes on her head and tore her robe. And putting her hand on her head, she went away crying bitterly.
passages.sermon:
Tamar was a daughter of King David.
Tamar was a virgin.
Tamar had just been disgraced by her brother Amnon.
Tamar put ashes on her head.
Tamar tore the robe of many colors she was wearing.
Tamar placed her hand on her head.
Tamar walked away.
Tamar cried out with a loud voice.
passages.original: וַתִּקַּ֨ח תָּמָ֥ר אֵ֙פֶר֙ עַל־ רֹאשָׁ֔הּ וּכְתֹ֧נֶת הַפַּסִּ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָלֶ֖יהָ קָרָ֑עָה וַתָּ֤שֶׂם יָדָהּ֙ עַל־ רֹאשָׁ֔הּ וַתֵּ֥לֶךְ הָל֖וֹךְ וְזָעָֽקָה׃

passages.text: Her brother Absalom said to her, “Has your brother Amnon been with you? Be quiet for now, my sister. He is your brother. Do not take this thing to heart.” So Tamar lived as a desolate woman in the house of her brother Absalom.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was Tamar’s brother.
Absalom spoke to Tamar.
Absalom said, “Did Amnon, your brother, do this to you?”
Absalom said, “Be quiet now, my sister.”
Absalom said, “He is your brother.”
Absalom said, “Do not let this matter trouble your heart.”
Tamar lived in Absalom’s house.
Tamar was desolate.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלֶ֜יהָ אַבְשָׁל֣וֹם אָחִ֗יהָ הַאֲמִינ֣וֹן אָחִיךְ֮ הָיָ֣ה עִמָּךְ֒ וְעַתָּ֞ה אֲחוֹתִ֤י הַחֲרִ֙ישִׁי֙ אָחִ֣יךְ ה֔וּא אַל־ תָּשִׁ֥יתִי אֶת־ לִבֵּ֖ךְ לַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַתֵּ֤שֶׁב תָּמָר֙ וְשֹׁ֣מֵמָ֔ה בֵּ֖ית אַבְשָׁל֥וֹם אָחִֽיהָ׃

passages.text: When King David heard all this, he was furious.
passages.sermon: King David was the ruler of Israel.\r\nHe heard everything that had happened.\r\nHe became very angry.
passages.original: וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֔ד שָׁמַ֕ע אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיִּ֥חַר ל֖וֹ מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: And Absalom never said a word to Amnon, either good or bad, because he hated Amnon for disgracing his sister Tamar.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was Tamar’s brother.
Amnon was also Tamar’s brother.
Amnon disgraced Tamar.
Absalom hated Amnon because of this.
Absalom never spoke to Amnon.
He did not say anything good to Amnon.
He did not say anything bad to Amnon.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ דִבֶּ֧ר אַבְשָׁל֛וֹם עִם־ אַמְנ֖וֹן לְמֵרָ֣ע וְעַד־ ט֑וֹב כִּֽי־ שָׂנֵ֤א אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶת־ אַמְנ֔וֹן עַל־ דְּבַר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִנָּ֔ה אֵ֖ת תָּמָ֥ר אֲחֹתֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: Two years later, when Absalom’s sheepshearers were at Baal-hazor near Ephraim, he invited all the sons of the king.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Two years passed.
Absalom had sheepshearers at Baal-hazor.
Baal-hazor was near Ephraim.
Absalom invited all the sons of King David.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ לִשְׁנָתַ֣יִם יָמִ֔ים וַיִּהְי֤וּ גֹֽזְזִים֙ לְאַבְשָׁל֔וֹם בְּבַ֥עַל חָצ֖וֹר אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִם־ אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיִּקְרָ֥א אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם לְכָל־ בְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: And he went to the king and said, “Your servant has just hired shearers. Will the king and his servants please come with me?”
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom went to King David.
Absalom spoke to King David.
Absalom said, “Your servant has hired shearers.”
Absalom asked, “Will the king and his servants come with your servant?”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּה־ נָ֥א גֹזְזִ֖ים לְעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ יֵֽלֶךְ־ נָ֥א הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וַעֲבָדָ֖יו עִם־ עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: “No, my son,” the king replied, “we should not all go, or we would be a burden to you.” Although Absalom urged him, he was not willing to go, but gave him his blessing.
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Absalom.
David was Absalom’s father and the king of Israel.
David said, “No, my son.”
David said, “We should not all go.”
David said, “We would be a burden to you.”
Absalom urged David to go.
David refused to go.
David gave Absalom his blessing.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶל־ אַבְשָׁל֗וֹם אַל־ בְּנִי֙ אַל־ נָ֤א נֵלֵךְ֙ כֻּלָּ֔נוּ וְלֹ֥א נִכְבַּ֖ד עָלֶ֑יךָ וַיִּפְרָץ־ בּ֛וֹ וְלֹֽא־ אָבָ֥ה לָלֶ֖כֶת וַֽיְבָרֲכֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: “If not,” said Absalom, “please let my brother Amnon go with us.” “Why should he go with you?” the king asked.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom spoke to his father, the king.
Absalom said, “If you will not come, please let my brother Amnon go with us.”
The king replied to Absalom.
The king asked, “Why should Amnon go with you?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם וָלֹ֕א יֵֽלֶךְ־ נָ֥א אִתָּ֖נוּ אַמְנ֣וֹן אָחִ֑י וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָ֥מָּה יֵלֵ֖ךְ עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: But Absalom urged him, so the king sent Amnon and the rest of his sons.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom insisted strongly to the king.
The king was David.
David agreed because Absalom urged him.
David sent Amnon with Absalom.
David also sent all his other sons with Absalom.
passages.original: וַיִּפְרָץ־ בּ֖וֹ אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אִתּוֹ֙ אֶת־ אַמְנ֔וֹן וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־ בְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

passages.text: Now Absalom had ordered his young men, “Watch Amnon until his heart is merry with wine, and when I order you to strike Amnon down, you are to kill him. Do not be afraid. Have I not commanded you? Be courageous and valiant!”
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom spoke to his young men.
He gave them a command.
He said, “Watch Amnon carefully.
Wait until Amnon feels happy from drinking wine.
When I tell you, strike Amnon.
Kill him.
Do not be afraid.
I am the one who commands you.
Be strong.
Be brave.”
passages.original: וַיְצַו֩ אַבְשָׁל֨וֹם אֶת־ נְעָרָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר רְא֣וּ נָ֠א כְּט֨וֹב לֵב־ אַמְנ֤וֹן בַּיַּ֙יִן֙ וְאָמַרְתִּ֣י אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם הַכּ֧וּ אֶת־ אַמְנ֛וֹן וַהֲמִתֶּ֥ם אֹת֖וֹ אַל־ תִּירָ֑אוּ הֲל֗וֹא כִּ֤י אָֽנֹכִי֙ צִוִּ֣יתִי אֶתְכֶ֔ם חִזְק֖וּ וִהְי֥וּ לִבְנֵי־ חָֽיִל׃

passages.text: So Absalom’s young men did to Amnon just as Absalom had ordered. Then all the other sons of the king got up, and each one fled on his mule.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom had young men who served him.
Absalom gave his young men an order.
The young men obeyed Absalom.
They did to Amnon exactly what Absalom told them to do.
Amnon was also a son of King David.
All the other sons of the king stood up.
Each son mounted his own mule.
Each son fled from the place.
passages.original: וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֞וּ נַעֲרֵ֤י אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ לְאַמְנ֔וֹן כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖ה אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיָּקֻ֣מוּ׀ כָּל־ בְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וַֽיִּרְכְּב֛וּ אִ֥ישׁ עַל־ פִּרְדּ֖וֹ וַיָּנֻֽסוּ׃

passages.text: While they were on the way, a report reached David: “Absalom has struck down all the sons of the king; not one of them is left!”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David had many sons.
Absalom was one of David’s sons.
Absalom had just ordered his young men to kill Amnon, another son of David.
While David’s sons were traveling, someone brought news to David.
The report said, “Absalom has killed all the king’s sons.
None of them remain.”
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ הֵ֣מָּה בַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְהַשְּׁמֻעָ֣ה בָ֔אָה אֶל־ דָּוִ֖ד לֵאמֹ֑ר הִכָּ֤ה אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ בְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְלֹֽא־ נוֹתַ֥ר מֵהֶ֖ם אֶחָֽד׃ס

passages.text: Then the king stood up, tore his clothes, and lay down on the ground; and all his servants stood by with their clothes torn.
passages.sermon:
King David heard the report about his sons.
King David stood up.
King David tore his clothes.
King David lay down on the ground.
All of King David’s servants stood nearby.
All the servants had torn their clothes.
passages.original: וַיָּ֧קָם הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וַיִּקְרַ֥ע אֶת־ בְּגָדָ֖יו וַיִּשְׁכַּ֣ב אָ֑רְצָה וְכָל־ עֲבָדָ֥יו נִצָּבִ֖ים קְרֻעֵ֥י בְגָדִֽים׃ס

passages.text: But Jonadab, the son of David’s brother Shimeah, spoke up: “My lord must not think they have killed all the sons of the king, for only Amnon is dead. In fact, Absalom has planned this since the day Amnon violated his sister Tamar.
passages.sermon:
Jonadab was the son of Shimeah.  
Shimeah was David’s brother.  
Jonadab spoke up.  
He said to King David, “My lord, do not think they have killed all the king’s sons.  
Only Amnon is dead.  
Absalom planned this.  
He planned it since the day Amnon violated his sister Tamar.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֡עַן יוֹנָדָ֣ב׀ בֶּן־ שִׁמְעָ֨ה אֲחִֽי־ דָוִ֜ד וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַל־ יֹאמַ֤ר אֲדֹנִי֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל־ הַנְּעָרִ֤ים בְּנֵֽי־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ הֵמִ֔יתוּ כִּֽי־ אַמְנ֥וֹן לְבַדּ֖וֹ מֵ֑ת כִּֽי־ עַל־ פִּ֤י אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ הָיְתָ֣ה שׂוּמָ֔ה מִיּוֹם֙ עַנֹּת֔וֹ אֵ֖ת תָּמָ֥ר אֲחֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So now, my lord the king, do not take to heart the report that all the sons of the king are dead. Only Amnon is dead.”
passages.sermon:
Jonadab spoke to King David.
Jonadab was the son of Shimeah, David’s brother.
Jonadab said, “My lord the king, do not believe the report that all your sons are dead.
Only Amnon is dead.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֡ה אַל־ יָשֵׂם֩ אֲדֹנִ֨י הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ אֶל־ לִבּוֹ֙ דָּבָ֣ר לֵאמֹ֔ר כָּל־ בְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מֵ֑תוּ כִּֽי־ אִם־ אַמְנ֥וֹן לְבַדּ֖וֹ מֵֽת׃פ

passages.text: Meanwhile, Absalom had fled. When the young man standing watch looked up, he saw many people coming down the road west of him, along the side of the hill. And the watchman went and reported to the king, “I see men coming from the direction of Horonaim, along the side of the hill.”
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom fled.
A young man was standing watch.
The young watchman looked up.
He saw many people.
These people were coming down the road.
The road was west of the watchman.
The people were coming along the side of the hill.
The watchman went to the king.
He reported what he saw.
He said, “I see men coming from the direction of Horonaim, along the side of the hill.”
passages.original: וַיִּבְרַ֖ח אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיִּשָּׂ֞א הַנַּ֤עַר הַצֹּפֶה֙ אֶת־ עֵינוֹ וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֨ה עַם־ רַ֜ב הֹלְכִ֥ים מִדֶּ֛רֶךְ אַחֲרָ֖יו מִצַּ֥ד הָהָֽר׃

passages.text: So Jonadab said to the king, “Look, the sons of the king have arrived! It is just as your servant said.”
passages.sermon: Jonadab spoke to the king.\r\nJonadab said, “Look, the king’s sons have arrived.”\r\nJonadab said, “It happened just as your servant said.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יֽוֹנָדָב֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הִנֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בָּ֑אוּ כִּדְבַ֥ר עַבְדְּךָ֖ כֵּ֥ן הָיָֽה׃

passages.text: And as he finished speaking, the sons of the king came in, wailing loudly. Then the king and all his servants also wept very bitterly.
passages.sermon:
The sons of the king entered the room.
They cried out loudly.
They wept.
King David was there.
All his servants were with him.
The king and his servants began to weep.
They wept with great sorrow.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ כְּכַלֹּת֣וֹ לְדַבֵּ֗ר וְהִנֵּ֤ה בְנֵֽי־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ בָּ֔אוּ וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ קוֹלָ֖ם וַיִּבְכּ֑וּ וְגַם־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וְכָל־ עֲבָדָ֔יו בָּכ֕וּ בְּכִ֖י גָּד֥וֹל מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: Now Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur. But David mourned for his son every day.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom fled from his home.
Absalom went to Talmai.
Talmai was the son of Ammihud.
Talmai was the king of Geshur.
David was Absalom’s father.
David mourned for his son every day.
passages.original: וְאַבְשָׁל֣וֹם בָּרַ֔ח וַיֵּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־ תַּלְמַ֥י בֶּן־ עַמִּיחוּר מֶ֣לֶךְ גְּשׁ֑וּר וַיִּתְאַבֵּ֥ל עַל־ בְּנ֖וֹ כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: After Absalom had fled and gone to Geshur, he stayed there three years.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom fled from his home.
Absalom went to Geshur.
Absalom stayed in Geshur for three years.
passages.original: וְאַבְשָׁל֥וֹם בָּרַ֖ח וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ גְּשׁ֑וּר וַיְהִי־ שָׁ֖ם שָׁלֹ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃

passages.text: And King David longed to go to Absalom, for he had been consoled over Amnon’s death.
passages.sermon:
King David was the ruler of Israel.
David missed his son Absalom.
David wanted to go to Absalom.
David felt comforted about Amnon’s death.
David no longer mourned for Amnon, because Amnon had died.
passages.original: וַתְּכַל֙ דָּוִ֣ד הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָצֵ֖את אֶל־ אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם כִּֽי־ נִחַ֥ם עַל־ אַמְנ֖וֹן כִּֽי־ מֵֽת׃ס
